done b82ab265, report /home/user/Nikaia/docs/briefs/b894-lent-argument-arms.md.report.md

#894 is fixed and pushed to `develop`. An `if` or `match` passed to a lent parameter, with one arm a view and another a newly made value, now compiles in Rust.

- **What it emits:** every arm is wrapped in one value that is created as the argument and lent, so it lasts through the call: `look(&*if c { Arm::View(t) } else { Arm::Own(P { .. }) })`. Text arms use the existing `either(..)` wrapper instead.
- **New runtime type:** `nikaia_std::arm::Arm` in a new module `crates/nikaia-std/src/arm.rs`. Unlike Rust's `Cow`, it does not need the struct to be cloneable.
- **Scope:** the rule applies only when at least one arm is a lent name. An arm that is `null`, a place of its own, or some other view leaves the argument to the existing rules. This keeps the code generated for `emit_pattern` unchanged.
- **Tests:** the new test `a_lent_argument_from_arms_view_and_new` covers `if` and `match`, declared `ref` and inferred lent, struct and `String`. Rustc refused 4 places in it on the unfixed compiler. With the fix, the project tests pass (186), the `it` filters plus the guard set pass (214), and clippy and the pre-push check are clean. Gate: green.
- **Changelog:** "An `if` or a `match` handed to a lent parameter whose arms are a view and a value made in the arm now lowers to code that compiles: every arm is lent through the call."

I found two other defects that are not part of this fix. Both pass `nikaia check` and then fail in rustc; probes are in the report's `Found:` line:
- `look(P { name: t.name + "!" })` where `t` is a `ref P`: the generated code moves out of `t.name`.
- An owned local passed as one arm of an `if` and used after the call gets moved into the arm, so the later use fails.

The test cache is 2.5 GB, with 18 GB free on the disk. One new cache entry is over 100 MB: `run-bundle/65d964130cc06fb2`, 293 MB.
